name: Leaf Spot
symptoms: Brown or black circular spots on leaves
Yellow halos surrounding the spots
Premature yellowing and leaf drop
Spots may merge into larger blotches over time
causes: Fungal pathogens — Cercospora, Alternaria, Septoria
Bacterial pathogens — Xanthomonas, Pseudomonas
Prolonged leaf wetness from overhead watering
Poor air circulation between plants
treatmentOrganic: Remove and destroy affected leaves immediately
Apply neem oil spray every 7 days during outbreaks
Spray copper-based organic fungicide weekly
Improve airflow by thinning dense growth
Apply compost tea as a foliar feed
treatmentChemical: Follow label dilution rates — do not over-apply
prevention: Water at soil level, never overhead
Space plants according to mature size for airflow
Rotate crops on a 2-3 year cycle
Mulch to prevent soil-splash onto leaves
Disinfect pruning tools between plants
Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet

name: Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, stems, and buds
Distorted or curled leaves
Yellowing and premature leaf drop
Reduced flowering and fruit yield
Stunted new growth
causes: Fungal pathogens in the Erysiphales order
High humidity with dry leaf surfaces
Crowded plantings and poor air circulation
Shaded conditions favouring spore germination
treatmentOrganic: Spray 1 tsp baking soda + 1 tsp horticultural oil per 1 L water weekly
Apply diluted milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water) every 7 days
Use potassium bicarbonate fungicide weekly
Prune affected leaves and discard (do not compost)
Increase sunlight exposure where possible
treatmentChemical: Rotate fungicide classes to prevent resistance
prevention: Plant resistant cultivars when available
Provide 6+ hours of direct sunlight
Avoid evening watering
Thin foliage for cross-ventilation
Apply preventative neem oil during humid periods

name: Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric dark-brown bullseye lesions on lower leaves first
Yellow halo surrounding each lesion
Defoliation progresses from the base upward
Stem cankers and sunken dark spots on fruit shoulders
Reduced yield and sunscald on exposed fruit
causes: Alternaria solani fungus (and A. tomatophila)
Warm humid weather (24-29 °C) with 6+ hours leaf wetness
Splash-borne conidia from soil and infected debris
Plant stress from poor nutrition, drought, or heavy fruit load
treatmentOrganic: Prune lower infected leaves to slow spread upward
Apply copper-based organic fungicide every 7 days
Spray Bacillus subtilis biofungicide preventatively
Mulch heavily to block soil-splash dispersal
Maintain plant nutrition — healthy plants resist better
treatmentChemical: Chlorothalonil every 7-10 days from first symptoms
Mancozeb on alternating schedule with chlorothalonil
Azoxystrobin as a translaminar option (rotate classes)
prevention: Plant resistant tomato/potato varieties
3+ year rotation away from solanaceous crops
Stake or cage plants to keep foliage off the ground
Water at soil level, never overhead
Destroy crop debris each autumn
Apply preventative sprays during humid weather

name: Late Blight
symptoms: Pale-green water-soaked lesions that expand quickly
White fuzzy sporulation on leaf undersides in humid weather
Brown-black blotches on stems and petioles
Firm brown leathery patches on fruits and tubers
Whole plants can collapse within days of first symptoms
causes: Phytophthora infestans oomycete
Cool wet weather (10-20 °C) with prolonged leaf wetness
Wind-borne spores travel up to 50 km from source
Persists on infected tubers and volunteer plants
treatmentOrganic: Remove and BURN infected plants immediately — never compost
Apply copper hydroxide every 5-7 days at first sign
Spray Bacillus subtilis biofungicide preventatively
Cull volunteer potatoes that emerge after harvest
Stake plants and mulch heavily
treatmentChemical: Fluazinam or famoxadone in commercial production
Phosphorous acid drench as a curative
prevention: Choose certified disease-free seed potatoes and transplants
Plant late-blight-resistant varieties (Mountain Magic, Sarpo)
Apply preventative copper sprays before rainy spells
Destroy cull piles and volunteer nightshades each spring
Monitor regional blight reports during cool wet weather
3+ year rotation away from solanaceous crops

name: Rust
symptoms: Orange, yellow, or reddish-brown pustules on leaf undersides
Corresponding yellow flecks on leaf upper surfaces
Premature defoliation in severe infections
Weakened plant vigor and reduced yield
Spore powder rubs off on fingers when touched
causes: Pucciniales fungi — many species, often host-specific
Warm humid conditions (60-75 °F / 15-24 °C) with leaf wetness
Wind-dispersed spores from nearby infected plants
Alternate hosts allowing the rust life cycle to complete
treatmentOrganic: Remove infected leaves at first sign and seal in bin (do not compost)
Spray sulphur dust on cool dry mornings
Apply neem oil every 7-10 days during outbreaks
Use compost tea to boost natural leaf microbiome
Prune for better airflow through the canopy
treatmentChemical: Myclobutanil on fruit trees and vegetables
Apply at first symptom — curative use is less effective
prevention: Select rust-resistant cultivars
Eliminate nearby alternate hosts (e.g. junipers near apples)
Avoid overhead watering
Space and prune for airflow
Clean up fallen leaves each autumn

name: Wilt
symptoms: Sudden wilting of leaves despite moist soil
Yellowing starting at lower leaves and moving upward
Brown vascular tissue visible when stem is cut
One-sided wilting on tomato/cucurbit plants
Plant death within days to weeks
causes: Fusarium oxysporum (fusarium wilt)
Verticillium dahliae (verticillium wilt)
Erwinia tracheiphila — vectored by cucumber beetles
Soil temperatures above 75 °F / 24 °C favour fusarium
Soil-borne — persists for years in infested soil
treatmentOrganic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Solarise soil with clear plastic in hot months
Inoculate seedlings with Trichoderma harzianum
Drench root zone with Bacillus subtilis solution
Increase soil organic matter to suppress pathogens
treatmentChemical: No effective curative chemicals — focus on prevention
Pre-plant soil fumigation with metam-sodium (commercial only)
Fungicide drenches with thiophanate-methyl as supportive treatment
prevention: Plant resistant varieties (look for VFN coding on tomatoes)
Rotate non-host crops for 4+ years
Sanitise tools and stakes between seasons
Use clean seed and certified transplants
Avoid over-fertilising with nitrogen
Control insect vectors (cucumber beetles) early

name: Root Rot
symptoms: Wilting despite wet soil
Yellowing lower leaves
Black, mushy, or slimy roots when uprooted
Foul rotting smell from the root ball
Stunted growth and plant decline
causes: Pythium, Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium fungi
Overwatering and poorly draining soil
Compacted soil restricting oxygen to roots
Reused contaminated pots or potting mix
treatmentOrganic: Stop watering and let soil dry partially
Remove plant, cut away black mushy roots with sterile blade
Repot in fresh well-draining mix with perlite/pumice
Drench with diluted hydrogen peroxide (1 tbsp / L) once
Apply mycorrhizal inoculant to encourage healthy roots
treatmentChemical: Thiophanate-methyl for general fungal root rot
prevention: Use pots with drainage holes
Choose well-draining substrate (avoid heavy clay)
Water only when top 2-3 cm of soil is dry
Sterilise reused pots with 10 % bleach solution
Raise garden beds for better drainage
Avoid burying stems below their original soil line

name: Anthracnose
symptoms: Sunken dark lesions on fruit, leaves, and stems
Pink or orange spore masses in lesion centres in humid weather
Premature fruit drop
Twig dieback on woody plants
Leaf curling and distortion on hosts like sycamore and mango
causes: Colletotrichum and Apiognomonia fungi
Warm humid conditions (60-80 °F / 15-27 °C)
Spread via rain splash and contaminated tools
Overwinters in fallen debris and bark cankers
treatmentOrganic: Prune affected branches 15 cm below symptoms
Disinfect tools with 70 % alcohol between cuts
Apply copper-based organic fungicide at bud-break
Mulch heavily to suppress soil-borne spores
Apply Bacillus amyloliquefaciens biofungicide
treatmentChemical: Chlorothalonil at first symptom, every 7-14 days
prevention: Plant resistant cultivars
Rake and destroy fallen leaves and fruit each autumn
Avoid overhead irrigation
Prune for airflow and sunlight penetration
Apply dormant copper spray on woody hosts

name: Black Spot
symptoms: Circular black spots on rose leaves with fringed edges
Yellow halos around spots, leaves turn yellow then drop
Defoliation starts on lower leaves and moves up
Weakened plants with sparse blooms
Cane lesions in severe cases
causes: Diplocarpon rosae fungus
Warm humid weather above 75 °F / 24 °C
Leaf wetness for 7+ continuous hours
Spores splash from infected debris on the soil
treatmentOrganic: Remove every infected leaf — including those on the ground
Spray 1 tbsp baking soda + 1 tsp horticultural oil per 4 L water weekly
Apply sulphur dust on cool dry mornings
Use neem oil every 7-10 days during humid periods
Mulch base with shredded bark to block spore splash
treatmentChemical: Rotate three different fungicide classes through the season
prevention: Plant black-spot-resistant rose varieties (Knock Out, Bonica)
Water at soil level in the morning
Provide 6+ hours of full sun
Prune for airflow each spring
Apply preventative dormant-oil + copper spray at bud-break
